output.brief:
The most likely cause is contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, the new pads or the hilly routes. Northfield Motor Services refilled 11 of the 13 Eastgate vans they serviced during the bay closure from an old, water-contaminated bulk drum. Two vans got fluid from a new drum. The two Northfield vans retested on 24 September had boiling points of about 150°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. All 11 vans with complaints were serviced by Northfield. Pad batches and Upper Wend days were spread evenly across the vans, and the same drivers reported nothing in other vans, including on Upper Wend. Northfield recommended rechecking the other vans on 25 September, and no reply is on file.

What to do this week:
- Pull the Northfield-serviced vans from service now. Test and renew their fluid from sealed stock. Do not wait for the fluid test before pulling them. The two new-drum vans can be tested and cleared.
- Do not issue warnings or run retraining. The complaints were accurate, and punishing them would stop drivers reporting.
- Hold off on switching pad suppliers. The squeal data is confounded and doesn't bear on this problem.
- Check whether any Calder Road Garage fluid is also suspect.

I am fairly confident. A fluid test on the other vans would confirm it.
